Stuckrath, C. and Worrell, E. (2022). Energy Efficiency and Cost Saving Opportunities for Distilleries: An ENERGY STAR Guide for Energy and Plant Managers. Document Number 430-R-21043, U.S. Environmental Protection Agency, Office of Air and Radiation, Washington, DC, February 2022. No DOI or URL printed.

Locators are printed page numbers (PDF page = printed + 3). An ENERGY STAR measure catalogue for beverage-spirits distilleries; almost every number is reprinted from other sources (Jacques et al. 2003, BIER 2012, U.S. DOE/IAC, case studies). Main file (30 process-technology rows): whole-distillery energy intensity from Jacques et al. 2003 (thermal 70-75 kBtu/gal and 0.7-1.0 kWh/gal, 200 proof) and the BIER 2012 benchmark (column 10-29, pot 29-110, average 34.4 kBtu/gal 80 proof), all converted to MJ (or kWh) per litre of PURE alcohol with the formula shown (80-proof figures divided by 0.4); bottling 0.6 (0.2-1.5) MJ per litre of 80-proof product (different basis, stated in note); mash cooker temperatures; MVR/TVR, Jameson vacuum+MVR and MGP pressure-cascade distillation (description, temperature, capacity, CO2 reduction); stillage dryer 1,350 Btu/lb water (3.14 GJ/t water), low-temperature belt dryer 1 kWh/kg water, single-effect evaporator 1 t steam/t water (all per t WATER, not product); Diageo AD plants (capacity, annual output); electric and electrode boilers, gas-turbine and engine CHP (HHV), CPC solar steam, biomass boiler CO2 cut; chillers (COP 6.4 high-efficiency vs 4.1 standard, centrifugal 0.2 GJ/GJ, absorption 1.6 GJ heat/GJ, optimized plant 0.64 kW/ton). Flows: grain input 2.674 kg per L pure alcohol (new commodity term grain). _measures.csv: quantified measures of Chapters 3-15 as printed (77 rows). _other-values.csv: sector statistics, the App. A/Ch.13 MJ/L restatements of BIER, byproduct moisture/solids, AD shares, TVR 25%, MVR opex 2-7% of capex, CO2 fuel coefficients (Table 4). Not loaded: Figures 13-16 (energy cost and pie-chart shares; slice labels not assignable from text), Table 6-8 industry tables, qualitative dryer comparisons (rotary direct-fired with gas recycle, ring, indirect-fired, steam-tube, superheated steam), multiple-effect/TVR/MVR evaporators, fermentation measures without numbers, lighting/HVAC tables. No cost rows in the main file: the guide gives no technology capex/opex.

(1) BIER 2012 figures are restated inconsistently: p.5 gives total distillery energy column 10-29 and pot 29-110 kBtu/gal (80 proof) with overall average 34.4; p.103 and p.137 restate them as distillation-process energy, column average 8.0 MJ/L (range 2.8-8.0, average equals maximum) and pot average 9.6 MJ/L, which equals the overall average 34.4 kBtu/gal. (2) Fuel share of energy cost: p.3 says 60% to 50%, p.139 says electricity rose from 35% to 50%. (3) p.5 electricity printed as 0.96-1.36 kBtu/gallon (80 proof) inside a kWh sentence. (4) Harpoon case p.70 converts a 20-30 degF rise to -6.6 to -1.1 degC; SolarWall 100 degF rise printed as 55 degC. (5) Jameson capacity 64 million liters/year without liquid basis; Diageo AD table MW figures without saying fuel, electric or thermal. (6) No price year for any cost (measures only). (7) Heating-value basis stated only for CHP (HHV).
